name: GrowLatam
tagline: A login-gated growth and outreach platform oriented toward Latin American markets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Everything public about this product is a login box, so treat this entry as provisional. The shape implied by the name, growth and outreach work aimed at LatAm markets, is mostly CRUD: contacts, segments, sequences, a pipeline board, some reporting. An agent can produce that in a weekend and it will feel fine for one person running their own list. What an agent cannot produce is whatever contact or company data sits behind the login, plus deliverability plumbing and any local compliance work, and if that data is the actual product then the DIY build is just an empty database with nice views.
coreLoopDIY: A local contact and pipeline tracker that imports CSV leads, segments them, tracks outreach stages, and drafts per-contact messages you send yourself.
requirements: a CSV export of the leads you already have
optional LLM API key if you want generated message drafts
your own email client or sending provider for anything actually going out
whatYouLose: Any proprietary lead or company data that lives behind the login
Email deliverability: warmup, domain reputation, bounce and unsubscribe handling
Local tax ID, language, and data protection handling for multiple LatAm jurisdictions
Shared pipeline for a team, with permissions and activity history
Someone to blame when the list goes stale
moatNotes: If the value is a curated LatAm contact or company dataset, no amount of local code recreates it. If the value is the workflow around your own list, it is a weekend.
whyPeopleStillPay: Regional growth tools sell two things at once: software and a head start. The software half is unremarkable and copyable. The head start, lists, local phone and tax formats, payment and messaging channels that matter in specific countries, integrations with CRMs people there already use, is the part that takes years and local presence to assemble. Teams pay because assembling that themselves is a hiring problem, not a coding problem.
notes: Rated on the shape of the category rather than the product, because the only public surface is a login wall.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user lead pipeline and outreach workspace. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/pipeline.db, migrations in plain SQL on boot.
- Server Actions for all mutations. No separate API layer.
- Runs with: npm install, npm run dev. Nothing else.

Data model:
- contacts: name, company, role, email, phone, country, locale, source, tags (comma string), notes, createdAt.
- stages: ordered list, seeded with new, contacted, replied, meeting, won, lost.
- contact_stage_events: contact id, stage id, note, occurredAt. Current stage is the latest event.
- messages: contact id, channel (email or whatsapp), subject, body, status (draft or sent), createdAt, sentAt.

Features, in scope:
- CSV import page: upload, map columns to fields, dedupe on email, show a preview and a count of skipped rows.
- Contacts table: search, filter by country, tag, and current stage. Bulk tag and bulk stage change.
- Contact detail page: fields, full stage history timeline, message list, quick note box.
- Pipeline board: columns per stage, drag a card to move it, which writes a stage event.
- Message drafting: a template system with {{name}}, {{company}}, {{role}} placeholders stored in the db. Render a per-contact draft, let the user edit it, then Copy to clipboard and mark as sent manually.
- Optional LLM draft: if OPENAI_API_KEY exists in .env, add a Draft with AI button that fills the body from the template plus contact notes. If the key is absent, hide the button, do not error.
- Dashboard: contacts per stage, new contacts per week, reply rate computed from stage events.
- CSV export of contacts with current stage.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Sending email or WhatsApp. Drafts are copied out by hand. Say so in the UI.
- Any bundled contact or company dataset. The user brings their own CSV.
- Multi-user, auth, roles, billing.

Deliver a README with setup, a .env.example containing only OPENAI_API_KEY, and a seed script that inserts 20 fake contacts so the board is not empty on first run.
